chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Abi Jamilah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ows, from Damrah ibn Abi Damrah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:
All decrees of the Muslims are executed in one of three ways: just testimony, a definitive oath, or a practice established with the Imams of Guidance.
ai.seo_question: What are the three ways Muslim legal decrees are established according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies testimony, definitive oaths, and the established practice of the Imams as the three pillars for validating Islamic rulings, highlighting the unique Shia emphasis on the Imams' living tradition as a source of law. This narration underscores the continuity between prophetic authority and the Imams' guidance, serving as a critical basis for usul al-fiqh in distinguishing between general customary practice and authoritative religious precedent.
